caption:
What actually changes at every level, from 400 to 2000. Save this for the next time you're stuck on a plateau. ♟️

Where are you on the ladder right now? 👇

#chess #chesstok #chesstips #chessimprovement #chessrating

slides.fix: Games here swing on missed mates and pieces moved for no reason. Knowing how to deliver checkmate turns half your winning positions into actual wins.
slides.habit: Practise mating with king and queen, then king and rook, until you can do it without thinking.

slides.fix: Before every move, ask what your opponent’s last move attacks. Most games here are lost to a piece left hanging, not to a clever plan.
slides.habit: Check every capture and every check, for both sides, before you touch a piece.

slides.fix: Knights and bishops out, king castled, rooks connected, all before you go hunting. Early queen raids stop working around here.
slides.habit: No piece moves twice in the opening unless it has to.

slides.fix: Forks, pins and skewers decide most games at this level. Pattern recognition beats calculation, and it only comes from volume.
slides.habit: Fifteen minutes of puzzles a day, every day.

slides.fix: Start asking what the position wants: which pawn break, which weak square, which piece is your worst. Then improve it.
slides.habit: Review every loss without an engine first. Find where your plan went wrong.

slides.fix: Games are won in rook endgames and lost in time trouble. The players who climb here convert small edges calmly.
slides.habit: Learn the key rook endgames, and never spend a third of your clock on one move.
